doc.title: Orrin Keepnews interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 7, 2002

chapter: Monk, the Army and learning the job
title: Was Monk hard to play with?
summary: He denies sidemen found Monk hard, since Monk chose people he knew could play his music.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with and understanding Thelonious Monk

blocks.x: Well Thelonious was apparently, in a lot of cases, hard to play with? Hard to get used to? Is that a fair statement?

No. Because first of all there was — working with Thelonious was not something that you did, I mean you being another musician, very arbitrarily or casually. If you were playing in a band with Monk or on a record date with Monk it was based on his awareness of you and his approval and his considering that it was likely that you would be able to perform his music. Because again, playing with Monk involved one of two things. Either playing Monk compositions or playing standards that he found he could adapt. So that the hard part sort of came first. It came before you got to the starting gate. I don’t think it’s fair to say that people found it hard playing with him. First of all people that were invited to play with him generally turned out to have the ability to do so. It was his judgement in the first place, and his judgment was pretty God damn — well look at the personnel situation. Look at how long a time, on the whole, individual sidemen worked with him. Yes some didn’t, changes were made here and there and various circumstances entered into it, but by and large it’s not like gee it’s hard to play with Monk and there’s some kind of revolving door there, that is absolutely not the case. © Fillius Jazz Archive -12-
